question: Who will be elected leader of the Senate Democratic Caucus in the 120th Congress?

calls.reasoning: Secret-ballot caucus vote Dec 1 (threshold reported as 28 or 29 votes). Public whip counts (counts vary by outlet): Schumer ~12-16 endorsements vs Van Hollen ~5-6, most uncommitted; Schumer claims he has the votes, Van Hollen claims ~15 incl. private pledges. Late momentum for VH (Slotkin, Troy Jackson endorsements; 3 freshmen oppose Schumer without endorsing VH). Base rate: incumbent Senate party leaders facing caucus challenges nearly always survive (e.g., Byrd 1984). Polymarket 'Next Senate Majority Leader' (~$2.07M volume) prices Schumer 93/VH 7/Schatz ~1. I couldn't read its full rules (it lists an end date of Nov 3, 2026, though the event is Dec 1). It asks about majority leader, not caucus leader, but with Democrats in the majority these should resolve the same in almost all cases, so I treat it as a close-match anchor. Thin vote-count buckets imply ~10% for Schumer under 28 votes. Shade slightly below the market for secret-ballot defection risk; small Other mass for a last-minute withdrawal or the vote slipping past Jan 3, 2027.
calls.reference_class: Challenges to sitting U.S. Senate party leaders in caucus leadership elections (e.g., Byrd 1984, other contested caucus leader votes)

calls.reasoning: Reference class: challenged incumbent congressional party leaders almost always survive (~90%). Markets: Kalshi 93/7/1 (Nov 20), Polymarket ~92/7/1 (Nov 26); Polymarket vote-count bins imply ~10% Schumer <28. Shaded slightly below markets for secret-ballot defection risk and a freshman class leaning anti-Schumer. Other (withdrawal/compromise like Schatz/postponement) ~2%.
calls.reference_class: Challenged incumbent congressional party leaders in caucus leadership elections (Daschle 1994, Reid, McConnell, Pelosi 2016/2018)

calls.reasoning: Base rate: challenged incumbent party leaders in caucus secret ballots (Pelosi 2016, McConnell 2022, etc.) almost always win (~90%). Whip counts as of Nov 20-27: Schumer ~17 public backers vs Van Hollen ~7-8 plus a few anti-Schumer; 28 of 55 needed, ~24-30 uncommitted. Schumer just led the caucus to a majority; Coons calls VH chances 'remote'. Markets: Kalshi 91% Schumer (~$6.5M), Polymarket 'Next Senate Majority Leader' 93/7/1 (~$2.1M) — near-match contract (majority leader post rather than the caucus vote itself; equivalent in practice given a Dem majority), and the thin vote-count brackets agree. Shaded ~3pts toward VH for secret-ballot defection risk and the large uncommitted freshman bloc; Other covers Schatz/compromise or the Dec 1 vote slipping past Jan 3 (no sign of delay).
calls.reference_class: Contested caucus/conference leadership elections where a sitting party leader is challenged (House/Senate, both parties, 1990s-2020s)
